# Glossary

Terms used across the Mailroom workspace. Each entry names the source it is taken from.

## Backend

A launch path adapter: OpenRouter, Modal with vLLM, Docker Compose, or a local Ollama or vLLM. It reports the fields it can; the rest are recorded as absent. A backend never changes the graph.

See also: [Run record](#run-record).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R5, "The launcher and backends")

## Blob

Anything with content (the original file, a transcript, a window, an extraction attempt, a verdict, the archived record, a human correction, a report), stored once under its SHA-256 and compressed. A document seen in many runs is stored once. Events hold only blob references, never document text.

See also: [Tombstone](#tombstone), [Run record](#run-record).

Source: docs/adr/0003-content-addressed-blobs-with-tombstones.md

## Client profile

Configuration for one client under `config/clients/<client>/`: its document classes, schemas, thresholds and label snapshot. A new document type is added by a client profile entry and plug-ins, with no code fork.

See also: [Routing policy](#routing-policy), [Prompt set](#prompt-set).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R4, R9)

## Closed label

A field of type label whose values come from a fixed vocabulary, such as cuad_family or urgency. After extraction, a value off its list routes the document to review with cause out_of_vocabulary; an absent value is valid.

See also: [Field type](#field-type), [Review bin](#review-bin).

Source: llm-mailroom src/config/taxonomy.yaml (label_vocabularies)

## Decision slot

A place in the graph where a decision model may be consulted. The eight slots of mailroom #309 are sorter reviewer, archive gate, judge replacement, judge check, boss check, arbiter veto, closed-field resolver and field review. Each is off by default, has its own caps, and is switched on in a policy or run spec. Every slot call is recorded as a decision event.

See also: [Routing policy](#routing-policy), [Event](#event).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R10)

## Dojo

The only place that scores a run, whatever backend produced it: pure functions from a run record plus labels to scores, statistics, projections and reports. It never runs a model and reads nothing but records and label files.

See also: [Run record](#run-record), [Label snapshot](#label-snapshot).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("The Dojo")

## Draw

The documents a run processes, recorded on the run. Runs that share a draw are compared paired by document.

See also: [Run record](#run-record).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("What a record holds", "Comparing runs")

## Event

One append-only entry per step of a run: run, document, sequence number, agent, attempt, kind (handoff, model call, decision, output, review, error), hashes of input and output, model, prompt id, tokens in, out and cached, price basis, latency, decision and cause token, previous hash and own hash.

See also: [Run record](#run-record), [Hash chain](#hash-chain).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("What a record holds")

## Field type

How an extracted field is scored: name, label, date, money, id, free_text, containment, cms_doc_ref, or entity_list, optionally with an element type (entity_list:name). The field_types and entity_element_types dictionaries list them.

See also: [Closed label](#closed-label).

Source: llm-dojo-scoring llm_dojo_scoring/scoring/field_scoring.py; llm-mailroom src/config/taxonomy.yaml

## Gold

A gold-label review decision, recorded with the reviewer's initials. Gold decisions sit on top of every other label layer.

See also: [Label status](#label-status).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R6, "Labels package")

## Hand-off

A typed envelope passed along an edge of the engine's graph: what the sender did, its confidence, references to the blobs it produced, and what it asks of the receiver. Every hand-off is an event in the run record, which is what makes behavior scorable.

Also called: handoff.

See also: [Event](#event), [Sorter](#sorter).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Agents and handoffs")

## Hash chain

Each document has its own chain of events within a run: `seq` starts at 0, the first event's `prev_hash` is GENESIS (64 zeros), and each event's `hash` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of every field except `hash`. Documents processed in parallel never wait on a shared chain lock.

See also: [Seal](#seal), [Event](#event).

Source: docs/adr/0002-per-document-hash-chains-and-chained-seals.md

## Hub

Ground truth published in the pinned mailroom dataset (Lucius-Morningstar/mailroom-dataset, by revision), less the labels the Dojo's label policy drops as stale.

See also: [Label status](#label-status).

Source: llm-dojo-scoring llm_dojo_scoring/schemas/label_policy.py; docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R6)

## Interim

A Claude-generated label built from gate-accepted, grounded extractions. A gap fill applies only where the Hub has no label; a correction applies only while the Hub value still equals the value it corrects; a disputed label is never applied.

See also: [Label status](#label-status).

Source: llm-dojo-scoring llm_dojo_scoring/schemas/label_policy.py

## Label snapshot

A committed, versioned file set of labels with a manifest hash. A run records the snapshot it was scored against, so a score is tied to the exact labels. A snapshot is checked against the dataset's content hashes and the closed label vocabularies before it is used; a document whose content hash does not match is flagged as unverified.

See also: [Label status](#label-status), [Closed label](#closed-label).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R6, "Labels package")

## Label status

The status every ground-truth label keeps, with its source: Hub, interim, near_gold or gold. Precedence is Hub, then interim, then near_gold, with gold reviewer decisions on top; it does not change. The label_statuses dictionary ranks them.

See also: [Hub](#hub), [Interim](#interim), [Near-gold](#near-gold), [Gold](#gold).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R6, "Labels package")

## Near-gold

A Claude-generated label from two agreeing passes or an Opus review. It fills only fields that neither the Hub nor an interim label covers.

Also called: near_gold.

See also: [Label status](#label-status).

Source: llm-dojo-scoring llm_dojo_scoring/schemas/label_policy.py

## Prompt set

A versioned set of agent prompts; `deploy_v1` is the default. A variant is an overlay on a prompt set that changes one agent's prompt, so two arms differ in exactly one prompt. Every model call records the id and hash of the prompt that ran.

See also: [Client profile](#client-profile).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Prompt optimization")

## Review bin

Where the pipeline parks a document for a person to review, with at least one review cause attached. A document must never be parked because of a provider outage: documents wait in the queue instead.

Also called: parked, review queue.

See also: [Review rate](#review-rate), [Closed label](#closed-label).

Source: llm-mailroom src/pipeline/bins.py (park_for_review) and src/pipeline/reconsideration.py; docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Failure handling")

## Review rate

Reviews over all documents of the pool.

See also: [Wrong archive](#wrong-archive), [Review bin](#review-bin).

Source: local-mailroom-sandbox src/mailroom_sandbox/job/gate.py

## Routing policy

A named, versioned file holding the engine graph's nodes, edges and their conditions, the thresholds, the decision-slot settings with their caps, and the retry budgets. Its hash is stored on every run, and it cannot change schemas or prompts. The `legacy` policy reproduces today's routing; each experiment arm is a policy.

Also called: policy.

See also: [Decision slot](#decision-slot).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Policies")

## Run record

The contract between the parts of the workspace: an append-only, hash-chained log of every step of a run, plus the blobs it references. It holds the run (id, kind, backend, policy name and hash, prompt set, agent-to-model map, label snapshot ids, draw, caps, who signed it), its events, its blobs and each document's version chain. The engine and launcher write it; the Dojo reads only it. The event log is the only source of truth; every index is derived from it.

Also called: record.

See also: [Event](#event), [Hash chain](#hash-chain), [Blob](#blob), [Seal](#seal).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("The run record and store"); docs/adr/0001-event-log-is-the-only-truth.md

## Scorable field

A field with a ground-truth label the Dojo can score an extraction against. A document archived with fewer labelled fields than the gate's minimum is an unscorable archive: no score is trusted and it is left out of the wrong-archive rate. Coverage (scorable documents and fields per class, by label status) is a first-class report.

See also: [Wrong archive](#wrong-archive), [Label status](#label-status).

Source: local-mailroom-sandbox src/mailroom_sandbox/job/gate.py; docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Labels package")

## Seal

A record that commits the head of every document chain in a run, the list of documents and the event count, chained to the previous seal. Experiment runs seal once at the end; service periods seal on a timer. Verification recomputes chains and seals, so an edited or deleted event, a deleted document or a cut tail fails.

See also: [Hash chain](#hash-chain).

Source: docs/adr/0002-per-document-hash-chains-and-chained-seals.md

## Sorter

The model-backed agent that classifies an incoming document into a document class (and subclass), then hands it off to the specialist tailored to that class. The engine keeps this sorter-to-specialist hand-off as its default graph shape; other shapes are policies.

See also: [Specialist](#specialist), [Hand-off](#hand-off).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R2 and R3, "The engine")

## Specialist

A model-backed agent tailored to one document class that extracts that class's fields against its extraction schema. A new document type brings a specialist prompt, or reuses a generic specialist with its schema.

See also: [Sorter](#sorter), [Field type](#field-type).

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md (R2 and R3, R4)

## Stage gate

The proof gate that ends a build stage and must pass before the next stage is trusted; for stage 1, the stored runs import cleanly, every chain verifies and both trace commands work. It runs end to end on the stored runs, in a script rather than in pytest.

Source: docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Build order and proof gates"); docs/test-strategy-record.md

## Tombstone

What deleting a blob's content leaves: a file recording the reason and time, in place of the content. The hash stays in the chain, so verification still passes; a blob that is simply gone fails verification and names the event.

See also: [Blob](#blob).

Source: docs/adr/0003-content-addressed-blobs-with-tombstones.md

## Utility

The per-document value a run is compared on. A correct archive is worth its extraction score; by default a review is worth -0.25, a wrong archive, a crash or a judge error -1.0, and an unscorable archive 0. The weights are set per study. A prompt or policy variant is kept on whole-pipeline utility and the wrong-archive rate at a fixed review rate.

See also: [Wrong archive](#wrong-archive), [Review rate](#review-rate).

Source: local-mailroom-sandbox src/mailroom_sandbox/autoresearch/scoring.py; docs/specs/2026-11-18-lean-rewrite-design.md ("Prompt optimization")

## Wrong archive

A document archived under another class than the expected one, or archived with an extraction score under the quality bar (0.90 by default). The wrong-archive rate is wrong archives over scorable archives.

See also: [Review rate](#review-rate), [Utility](#utility), [Scorable field](#scorable-field).

Source: local-mailroom-sandbox src/mailroom_sandbox/job/gate.py and src/mailroom_sandbox/autoresearch/scoring.py
